```{r}
# --- 2. Vectors ---

numeric_vector <- c(gravity, temperature, diameter, atmosphere_density,
                    num_moons, num_species, crystal_mountains)

# Sequence vector: 20 to 100 by 10

logical_vector <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), size = 10, replace = TRUE)

# Display
cat("Numeric vector:\n"); print(numeric_vector)
cat("\nSequence vector:\n"); print(sequence_vector)
cat("\nLogical vector:\n"); print(logical_vector)
cat("\n\n")
```

```{r}
                        dimnames = list(
```

```{r}
# --- 2.3 Investigating Your Data Frame ---

# Create a small Zephyria data frame
zephyria_df <- data.frame(
  region = c("North", "South", "East", "West", "Central"),
  population = c(500, 1200, 800, 150, 2300),
  avg_temp = c(-70, -60, -80, -75, -65),
  is_habitable = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)
)

cat("\nFirst 3 rows of zephyria_df:\n")
print(head(zephyria_df, 3))

cat("\nValue from 4th row, 1st column:\n")
print(zephyria_df[4, 1])

cat("\nLogical column (is_habitable):\n")
print(zephyria_df$is_habitable)

# Logical subsetting
cat("\nSubset: rows with population > 1000\n")
df_subset <- zephyria_df[zephyria_df$population > 1000, ]
print(df_subset)

# Subsetting by category
cat("\nSubset: rows from North and West regions\n")
df_subset_2 <- zephyria_df[zephyria_df$region %in% c("North", "West"), ]
print(df_subset_2)
```
```{r}
# --- 2.4 Handling “Corrupted” Data (NA) ---

# Create a copy
df_corrupted <- zephyria_df

# Introduce 3 NAs
df_corrupted[2, 2] <- NA
df_corrupted[4, 3] <- NA
df_corrupted[5, 4] <- NA

cat("\nCorrupted data frame:\n")
print(df_corrupted)

# Count total missing values
cat("\nTotal missing values:\n")
print(sum(is.na(df_corrupted)))

# Count missing values per column
cat("\nMissing values per column:\n")
print(colSums(is.na(df_corrupted)))

# Mean of numeric column with NA
cat("\nMean of 'population' (ignoring NA):\n")
print(mean(df_corrupted$population, na.rm = TRUE))

# Remove rows with NAs
cat("\nClean data frame (rows without NA):\n")
df_clean <- na.omit(df_corrupted)
print(df_clean)
```
```{r}
# --- 2.5 Bonus Challenge: which() ---

cat("\nRow with highest population:\n")
highest_pop_index <- which.max(zephyria_df$population)
print(zephyria_df[highest_pop_index, ])

cat("\nRow with lowest population:\n")

print(zephyria_df[lowest_pop_index, ])
```

```{r}
#  Task 3: Real-World Dataset: Penguins


# 3.1 The Quest: Find Your Data
# Data from: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/master/inst/extdata/penguins.csv

# Make sure the file "penguins.csv" is in your project directory.


# 3.2 The Import: Load Your Data
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

penguins <- read_csv("penguins.csv")

# First Inspection
cat("\n--- Penguin Dataset Structure ---\n")
glimpse(penguins)

cat("\n--- First Rows ---\n")
head(penguins)

cat("\n--- Statistical Summary ---\n")
summary(penguins)



#        Task 3.3 — dplyr Exploration


# 5 questions using all required dplyr verbs:
# select(), filter(), arrange(), mutate(), group_by(), summarise()


# Question 1:
# Which penguin species has the largest average body mass?


cat("\n\nQ1: Largest Average Body Mass by Species:\n")
penguins %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(avg_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_mass)) %>%
  print()



# Question 2:
# Select only species, island, and bill length columns.


cat("\n\nQ2: Selected Columns (species, island, bill_length_mm):\n")
penguins %>%
  select(species, island, bill_length_mm) %>%
  head() %>%
  print()



# Question 3:
# Which penguins have a bill length greater than 50 mm?


cat("\n\nQ3: Penguins With Bill Length > 50 mm:\n")
penguins %>%
  filter(bill_length_mm > 50) %>%
  select(species, island, bill_length_mm) %>%
  arrange(desc(bill_length_mm)) %>%
  print()



# Question 4:
# Create a new column: body_mass_kg (grams → kilograms).


cat("\n\nQ4: Add body_mass_kg Column:\n")
penguins %>%
  mutate(body_mass_kg = body_mass_g / 1000) %>%
  select(species, body_mass_g, body_mass_kg) %>%
  head() %>%
  print()



# Question 5:
# How many penguins are recorded per island?


cat("\n\nQ5: Penguin Counts per Island:\n")
penguins %>%
  group_by(island) %>%
  summarise(count = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(count)) %>%
  print()
```
```{r}


# TASK 4: FUNCTION TOOLKIT
# Dataset: penguins (CSV from GitHub)


# --- Load libraries ---
library(readr)
library(dplyr)




# 4.1 GREETING FUNCTION


welcome_to_my_universe <- function( universe_name, your_name) {
  cat("-----------------------------------------\n")
  cat(" Welcome to the Analysis Toolkit for:", universe_name, "\n")
  cat(" Report prepared by:", your_name, "\n")
  cat("-----------------------------------------\n")
}

# Call the greeting function
welcome_to_my_universe("Penguin Research Universe", "Your Name")




# 4.2 LOADING + INSPECTION FUNCTION


load_and_inspect <- function(file_path) {
  
  data <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  
  cat("\n--- Data Loaded Successfully ---\n")
  cat("File:", file_path, "\n\n")
  
  cat("--- Structure (glimpse): ---\n")
  print(glimpse(data))
  
  cat("\n--- First 6 Rows ---\n")
  print(head(data))
  
  return(data)
}

# Load dataset from URL
penguin_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/master/inst/extdata/penguins.csv"
my_data <- load_and_inspect(penguin_url)




# 4.3 QUERY FUNCTION
# Example: filter penguins heavier than X grams


filter_penguins_by_weight <- function(data, weight_threshold) {
  
  result <- data |>
    filter(body_mass_g > weight_threshold) |>
    select(species, island, body_mass_g)
  
  return(result)
}

# Call the query function
heavy_penguins <- filter_penguins_by_weight(my_data, 4500)
print(heavy_penguins)




# 4.4 REPORTING FUNCTION
# Summary report for one species


generate_report <- function(data, species_name) {
  
  # Filter for selected species
  species_data <- data |>
    filter(species == species_name)
  
  # Summary statistics
  avg_mass <- mean(species_data$body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE)
  avg_bill_length <- mean(species_data$bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
  min_flipper <- min(species_data$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_flipper <- max(species_data$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
  record_count <- nrow(species_data)
  
  # Print formatted report
  cat("\n--------------------------------------\n")
  cat(" Penguin Report for:", species_name, "\n")
  cat("--------------------------------------\n")
  cat(" Records found:", record_count, "\n")
  cat(" Average body mass:", round(avg_mass, 1), "g\n")
  cat(" Average bill length:", round(avg_bill_length, 1), "mm\n")
  cat(" Minimum flipper length:", min_flipper, "mm\n")
  cat(" Maximum flipper length:", max_flipper, "mm\n")
  cat("--------------------------------------\n\n")
}

# Call reporting function for two species
generate_report(my_data, "Adelie")
generate_report(my_data, "Gentoo")


```
